items.rationale: The indoor heating-pipe failure falls under §2.4.3(a). Under §§7.1.5 and 7.1.9, the 6.4 m line is capped at the ordinary copper equivalent for the repaired run, about €15/m gross.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow the equivalent plain copper fittings, not the chrome premium. Four standard elbows at about €10 each give €40.
Section 7.1.9 caps matching fittings used in the repair at the standard copper price. Five elbows at about €20 each give €100, subject to attribution to the repaired run under §7.1.8(e).
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow about €20 for one equivalent standard copper elbow used in the repair.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers ordinary repair fasteners. Case 40 supports about €9 gross for eight screws.

Section 7.1.8(e) excludes dimensions that do not correspond to the documented repair; no 10 mm pipe is identified. If the clamps are shown to be necessary repair fixings under §7.1.7(c), four would cost about €20.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers attributable pipe supports. Case 40 supports about €24 gross for four clamps of this size.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary labour for the ordinary pipe repair, not time spent on new additions under §7.1.9. Case 40 supports a ceiling near 6.75 hours × €90 gross for comparable repair work.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper time for the standard cut-out and reinstatement, not the upgrade work. Case 40 supports about 5.75 hours × €68 gross for comparable repair work.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 cap the line at the cost of reinstating the original rock-wool insulation. Six standard shells at about €20 each give €120.
Section 7.1.7(c) allows ordinary binding wire as a repair consumable, including on a standard rock-wool reinstatement basis. Case 40 supports about €19 for 2 kg.
Section 7.1.9 excludes installations not present before the loss. The new sensor has no pre-loss equivalent to indemnify.
Section 7.1.9 excludes the newly added valve because it did not replace any pre-loss component.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) permit a lump sum for minor materials attributable to the standard repair. Case 40 supports about €34 gross.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge per contractor per invoice. One charge at €73 gross is consistent with Case 40.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover disposal of the removed affected pipe and insulation. Case 40 places comparable small-job disposal near €60 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes administrative or processing fees billed on top of itemised labour and materials.
